meta.title: M1 — five dark core packages
meta.description: Five core/* packages merged from PR #203 on 2026-09-26: what each duplicates, and what to do with it.

provenance.agent: Claude Code · Opus 5.5 · audit burn-down session 3

props.title: 5 packages, 5 existing owners
props.subtitle: Each package re-implements something Lev already has. Pick per card, add a note if you like, then Copy JSON back into the chat.

props.content:
- **Source:** all 5 came from PR #203 (merge `a6716bf4c`, 09-26 04:17). The branch was authored 03-31 to 04-04.
- **Not built by anything:** none of the 5 is in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. So turbo and CI never typecheck or test them.
- **No users:** 0 code imports anywhere in core, plugins, apps, tests or tooling. The only mention is a dependency string in `plugins/hands/config.yaml:21`.
- **4 of 5 fail typecheck** with the same missing `@lev-os/domain/event-source.js` import (re-run: `core/a2a` tsc gives TS2307).
- **Original intent:** the OpenFang intake decided *EXTRACT + MONITOR*, meaning "inform" existing Lev owners, not add new packages (`workshop/analysis/openfang/analysis.md:141-152`).
- **Tests I re-ran:** vault 31/31, guardrails 5/5, flowmind-memory 15/15 (bun), security 25/25 (bun).
- **Keep:** `core/poly/src/formatters/toon.ts` came from the same PR, but R4 (fold TOON into output modes) now depends on it.
- **OK1:** the 5 specs stay on hold until these cards are decided.

items.title: core/a2a — in-memory agent-to-agent protocol
items.insight: Lev already has **three** A2A owners. This package would be the fourth, and it has no transport, no tests and no users.

options.label: Converge then delete
options.desc: Fold the Agent Card shape into the poly-compiler projection. Record the A2A task-state list as a requirement for a future poly a2a surface. Delete the package.

options.label: Re-home as poly a2a surface
options.desc: Move the card server into a core/poly a2a adapter, but only once a real outside A2A caller exists

options.label: Delete outright
options.desc: The design spike and the OpenFang analysis stay as the record

options.label: Keep as core/a2a
options.desc: Join the workspace, fix the import, write a spec. This makes a fourth A2A owner.

items.title: core/agent-fs — per-agent mounted folders in TypeScript
items.insight: The approved owner is **crates/lev-agentfs** (Rust, with a TS SDK). Its spec already covers mounts, copy-on-write overlays and sandboxing.
items.detail:
- Contents: `MountEngine` creates a session folder with project/reference/scratch/memory/output mounts, byte and file quotas, and a path-traversal guard. 843 LOC, 0 tests.
- Owner: `docs/specs/spec-agentfs.md` (`lifecycle_state: approved`). The glossary term is `env-agentfs`.
- It does raw directory I/O itself (readdir/mkdir/rm) instead of going through `core/file`.
- New ideas worth keeping: the five mount types and the per-session quotas.

options.label: Add delta to spec-agentfs, then delete
options.desc: Record mount types and quotas as requirements in the agentfs spec, then delete the TS package

options.label: Delete outright
options.desc: crates/lev-agentfs already does mount, overlay and sandbox

options.label: Thin TS adapter over agentfs-sdk
options.desc: Rewrite as a wrapper around the Rust SDK. Only worth it when a TS caller needs it; none does today.

items.title: core/credential-vault — encrypted secret store
items.insight: **plugins/vault** already ships (`ships-with: true`) with AES-256-GCM, scrypt, expiry, rotation, revoke and audit. Its tests are green (31/31, re-run).
items.detail:
- Contents: one `.enc` file per secret, an append-only event log, and per-secret `allowedAgents` plus a revoked set. OAuth2 PKCE is an interface only. 743 LOC, 0 tests.
- The one real addition is the per-agent allowlist gate (`vault-gates.ts:21-29`). plugins/vault scopes by graph depth instead.
- OpenFang intent: "Extract credential vault design → inform auth architecture" (analysis.md:151).

options.label: Port allowlist into plugins/vault, then delete
options.desc: Add the per-agent allowlist as an option next to depth scoping, then delete the package

options.label: Delete outright
options.desc: plugins/vault already covers everything else

options.label: Promote vault to core
options.desc: Merge plugins/vault into a new core credential owner. This mints an owner name, so it needs its own ruling.

items.title: core/flowmind-memory — MEMORY.md-style index with write rules
items.insight: **core/memory** already owns store, recall, decay and consolidation. The new part is the **write rules**: reject facts derivable from code, decay stale entries, cap the size. Tested 15/15.
items.detail:
- `dna/core/memory.dna.yaml:24`: "Memory owns the semantic memory API". The memory package already has decay (`memory-decay-manager.js`) and a `consolidate()` port.
- `ConsolidationReport` would mean two different things in two packages.
- The name is misleading: it imports nothing from flowmind.
- Your own memory practice (derivable facts, staleness) shows the write rules are wanted.

options.label: Move write rules into core/memory, then delete
options.desc: Port the derivability, staleness and budget rules plus their 15 tests as memory write admission. Drop the duplicate recall and the hand-written YAML parser.

options.label: Delete outright
options.desc: Keep the design spike as the record of the idea

options.label: Keep as a separate package
options.desc: Rename it, join the workspace, write a spec. Still a second memory owner.

items.title: core/security — seven security pieces in one package
items.insight: Five of the seven pieces duplicate an existing owner. One (a universal `Receipt` type) breaks the one-brain rule. Only **taint tracking** and the **SSRF URL check** are new.

options.label: Split: taint + SSRF to guardrails, delete the rest
options.desc: Move the two new pieces and their tests into plugins/guardrails as detectors, then delete the package

options.label: Delete outright
options.desc: Keep the security-stack design spike as the record; extract again when something needs it

options.label: New bounded context core/security
options.desc: Strip the duplicates and register a core security owner for information-flow control. This mints a name, so it needs its own ruling.

items.title: .lev/tmp — 7 tracked files inside an ignored folder
items.insight: `.lev/tmp/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:191`). But the old branch predated that rule, so the merge brought in 7 **tracked** files.
items.detail:
- `gap-analysis-report.md` is the branch's own audit: "the DNA is decorative, not structural" (4 FATAL / 8 ERROR / 11 WARNING).
- 5 matrix flows drive the packages above. One of them, matrix-004, fails `lev flowmind validate`.
- `matrix-architect-brief.md` is a "hidden" eval brief committed where agents can read it.

options.label: Untrack all; keep the gap report in .lev/pm/reports
options.desc: Move the gap report next to the same PR's cohesion report and untrack the rest so the ignore rule holds

options.label: Untrack all 7
options.desc: Rely on git history as the record

options.label: Leave as is
options.desc: Tracked files stay inside an ignored folder

items.title: Everything else PR #203 added
items.insight: Files outside the 5 packages were built around them. They should follow the package decisions.
items.detail:
- `plugins/hands`: 8 files, also outside the workspace; declares `@lev-os/flowmind-memory`.
- `.lev/matrix/`: 6 files (scenarios 1–5 plus a README).
- `docs/design`: 4 spikes. `docs/reports/cohesion-agentfs-flowmind.yaml`.
- `.lev/pm`: 2 designs, 3 intake records, 2 draft plans, 1 report.

options.label: Follow the package decisions
options.desc: Delete the drivers of deleted packages. Keep design spikes as records and mark them superseded.

options.label: Audit each separately
options.desc: Treat plugins/hands as its own M-card later

options.label: Keep all as records
options.desc: Annotate only

items.title: The 5 specs held under OK1
items.insight: If a package converges and is deleted, its spec belongs in the **owner's** spec as an amendment, not in a new file.
items.detail: - Owner specs that would be amended: `spec-poly-compiler` (Agent Card), `spec-agentfs` (mounts/quotas), plugins/vault README/spec (allowlist), `spec-memory` (write rules), guardrails (taint/SSRF).

options.label: Amend owner specs only
options.desc: No new spec files for deleted packages

options.label: Write the 5 specs anyway
options.desc: Record them as specs of deleted packages
